messages:
Eli Park: Quick sync — need to lock POC scope + capacity for ACME Health. They want a 4-week pilot, in-app clinician assistant + retrieval. Can we confirm success criteria, token budget, and GPU sizing by EOD?
Samira Khan: Yep. Two immediate asks: 1) success criteria (latency, quality), 2) rough cost + GPU recommendation.
Diego Mendez: For retrieval+generation, what avg prompt/response sizes are we assuming? That drives token math.
Eli Park: They gave sample traffic: 120 daily users (clinicians) during business hours, peak concurrency ~20 active sessions, expect ~10 queries per session/day. Avg prompt ~450 tokens, avg model reply ~900 tokens.
Olga Petrov: Ok rough numbers: 120 users * 10 q = 1,200 queries/day. Tokens/day = 1,200*(450+900)=1,620,000 tokens/day. p95 latency target is <= 300ms for short Qs, <= 800ms for long answers.
Samira Khan: On quality: ACME wants >85% pass rate on an internal eval set (50 representative prompts) and no safety failures. They also want logs for every inference + redaction controls.
Diego Mendez: For throughput, to support 20 concurrent active sessions with UI interactivity, aim for sustained 40 req/s and spike capacity up to 80 req/s. With avg 900 tokens output, that's ~36k tokens/s at sustained.
Eli Park: Can you translate that into GPU counts and a cost estimate? They have a hard cap of $10k for the pilot infrastructure.
Diego Mendez: Quick estimate: using a quantized 13B variant (vfast profile) on A10-like instances we can get ~50-70 tok/s per GPU for 900-token outputs with batching optimizations. So sustained 36k tok/s / 60 tok/s ≈ 600 GPUs — that can't be right for a POC. Need to sanity-check: I mixed tok/s vs token per request. Recalc: 40 req/s * 900 tok output = 36k tok/s total. But per GPU throughput expressed in req/s is better. If a GPU can do ~6 requests/s at 900 tokens (with batching), then need ~7 GPUs for sustained 40 req/s (40/6 ≈ 6.7). For spikes to 80 req/s, plan for 12 GPUs (with autoscale).
Samira Khan: That sounds reasonable. Can we aim for 2x autoscale headroom and a burst policy to fall back to a smaller model to save cost?
Diego Mendez: Yes — recommend primary: quantized 13B vfast, fallback: 7B distilled for overflow. Autoscale target: base 4 GPUs (handles ~24 req/s), scale to 12 for spikes.
Olga Petrov: Cost calc: assume per-GPU cost (cloud reserved POС rate) $1.50/hr for A10-equivalent on Dedicated pilot pricing (discounted). 4 GPUs base = 6$/hr -> 144$/day. Peak average (scaled to 8 GPUs during bus hours) ~12$/hr = 288$/day. Over 30 days ~4.3k - 8.6k. Add token egress/metadata costs ~est $1k. Total pilot infra ~6k-10k. Within their $10k limit if we tune.
Eli Park: Perfect — include SD (SLA) note: they require 99% uptime SLA during business hours and SOC2 questions.
Samira Khan: Ops notes: we need security checklist done (SCC + data flows). Olga can you own the questionnaire and ask Security for whiteboard?
Olga Petrov: I'll own it. Expect the pre-signed ATO doc set by tomorrow. Also need clarification on PHI handling — they want no raw logs stored in vendor plane. We'll propose client-side redaction and customer-managed KMS.
POC Bot: Reminder: POC onboarding checklist created: /playbooks/pocs/acme-health. Items: eval-suite upload, sample corpus, SLA doc, infra estimate.
Eli Park: Action items: (1) Diego — finalize GPU counts & fallback perf numbers with a quick perf run (2) Olga — start security questionnaire answers + KMS options (3) Samira — draft SOW and pilot pricing tiers (4) Me — coordinate customer expectations and ask for the 50-eval prompt set. Can we update by EOD?
Diego Mendez: I'll run a perf harness today. Quick local command I'll run and share numbers:
```
# perf harness (example)
./run_infer_load --model redwood-13b-vfast --batch-size 8 --seq-in 450 --seq-out 900 --concurrency 80 --duration 600
```
I'll post the results here when done.
Olga Petrov: Starting sec questionnaire now. If we propose client-side redaction, need to confirm SDK integration time ~1-2 days.
Samira Khan: Draft SOW: 4-week POC, base configuration (4 GPUs + autoscale to 12), 2 eval cycles, support hours M-F 9-5. I'll drop numbers and two pricing options (dedicated vs hosted credits) by 1630 PST.
Eli Park: Great — thanks team. If we hit cost >$10k, propose shortening pilot to 3 weeks or lowering base GPUs to 2 with heavier fallback usage.
Diego Mendez: Got it. Will aim to validate 4 GPU baseline can hit ~24 req/s. If not, note scaling requirements.
Samira Khan: I'll also pull historical token pricing and produce a per-req and per-day cost table.
Eli Park: Thanks — please ping me with any blockers.
Samira Khan: ping — SOW draft posted: https://redwood.atlassian/…/ACME-POC-SOW (comments welcome) :thumbsup:
Diego Mendez: Perf run complete — 4 GPU baseline gives ~22 req/s at 900 tokens with 8 batch size, p95 latency ~420ms. Posting raw logs in channel in 10.
Eli Park: Nice. We'll iterate on batch sizing. Next sync 0900 tomorrow with Security and Sales Ops.
Olga Petrov: Security questionnaire initial answers uploaded to drive. Flag: customer insists on no vendor-side full-text logs; proposing tokenized hashes + customer KMS.
POC Bot: Checklist update: perf results attached, SOW posted, sec answers uploaded.
Eli Park: Closing notes — looks within budget but sensitive to concurrency. We'll present two options to ACME: conservative (2 GPUs + heavy fallback, ~3k) and performance (4 GPUs + autoscale, ~6-8k).
